actions.describe: Asks how their day is going.
Asks whether they like animals or have pets.
Asks whether they have heard of the charity or the issue.
First problem point: animals surrendered or abandoned with nowhere to go.
Second problem point: shelters are full and animals get turned away.
Bridges from the problem to the solution.
Tells the impact story: rescued animals find a home.
Says others are already on board.
Trial close: a small agreement question.
Assumptive close: proceeds as if they have decided.
Asks for their last name to start the sign-up.
Indifferent close: gives the donor control of amount and frequency.
Confirms the donor believes in the cause.
Talks in general terms. No picture and no question.
Lists programs or facts. No feeling and no question.
Asks in a tentative, apologetic way.
Celebrates the sign-up in front of the donor.

criteria.label: Asked a question in your first turn
Said who you are and who you are out with
Opened with a real observation or an open question
Asked a question with a problem point
Layered at least two impulse factors
Used more than one closing method
Did not close before the Problem and Solution had landed
Confirmed they believe in the cause
Never talked thirty seconds without a question
Did not talk over an interruption

fake_compliment.label: Fake compliment. The manual calls this a non-negotiable.

pushed_after_no.label: Kept asking after the donor said they genuinely could not help.

fake_compliment.title: You complimented something that was not there.

pushed_after_no.title: She had told you she genuinely could not help, and you asked again.

kill.title: You talked for more than thirty seconds without a question.

closed_early.title: You asked before the Problem and Solution had landed.

close_below_line.title: You closed while she was below the Buying Line.

reclose_unhandled.title: You asked again without dealing with her objection.

reclose_same.title: You re-closed with the same method that triggered the objection.

talked_over.title: Something inside pulled her attention and you kept going.

drift.title: You talked without giving her anything to react to.

lost_attention.title: She dropped below the Attention Line and stayed there.

genuine_no.title: Three asks did not land, and she told you she could not help.

left_before_details.title: She said yes, and you left before finishing the sign-up.

walked_away.title: You walked away while the conversation was still alive.

left_well.title: You left without asking for the commitment enough times.

objection_handled.title: You deflected the objection and rebuilt her impulse.

agreed.title: You asked, and she said yes.

vague.title: You spoke in general terms and gave her nothing to react to.

program_list.title: You listed programs. She heard words and felt nothing.

tentative_close.title: You asked as if you expected a no.

celebrated_early.title: You celebrated while she was still at the door.

introduction: Hey, how is your day going? I love the bottlebrush by the door. I'm Alex, out with Placeholder Animal Rescue today. Have you heard much about what they do?
problem: Honestly, the part that got me is how many animals are surrendered with nowhere to go. Have you heard much about that?
And the shelters are full, so some get turned away. That's terrible, right? But there is hope.
solution: The rescued animals stay with foster carers until they find a home. Pretty incredible, right?
A lot of your neighbours have already jumped on board, and without ongoing support the foster program can't continue.
close: So that's the reason we are out here. The rescue relies on regular support, so I assume we can count on your support too, yeah?
What works best for you, monthly or annually?
It's completely up to you. You choose an amount that works.
objection: I hear you. Can I ask, does the idea of what they are doing make sense to you?
Exactly, and that is why most people start small. What works best for you, monthly or annually?
You'd be directly helping an animal off the street, and it's completely up to you. You choose an amount that works.
consolidation: Brilliant, you are going to be making a real difference. Let me get you set up. What was your last name?
And what works best for you, monthly or annually?
Out of curiosity, what was the main reason you decided to jump on board?
Thanks so much. Have a great day.
leave: No worries at all. Thanks for your time, have a great day.

introduction.label: Practise the Introduction
introduction.brief: Walk up, knock and introduce yourself. Get her talking within the first ten seconds.

problem.label: Practise the Problem
problem.brief: You have introduced yourself and she is listening. Give her the two problem points, a question with each, then bridge to the solution.
prelude: Hey, how is your day going? I love the bottlebrush by the door. I'm Alex, out with Placeholder Animal Rescue today. Have you heard much about what they do?

solution.label: Practise the Solution
solution.brief: She has heard the problem. Tell the impact story, layer two impulse factors and check in. Watch for the buying sign.
prelude: Hey, how is your day going? I love the bottlebrush by the door. I'm Alex, out with Placeholder Animal Rescue today. Have you heard much about what they do?
Honestly, the part that got me is how many animals are surrendered with nowhere to go. Have you heard much about that?
And the shelters are full, so some get turned away. That's terrible, right? But there is hope.

close.label: Practise the Close and the deflect
close.brief: She is above the Buying Line. Ask for the commitment. When she objects, deflect: acknowledge, confirm, re-impulse, then re-close a different way.

consolidation.brief: She has just said yes. Reinforce her decision, finish the sign-up, ask the self-justification question and leave warm.
